key_destruction_note: CRITICAL, fixed 2026-09-22. KeyManager.load_or_create branched on `st_size > 100`, so a raw 32-byte unprotected key never matched the load path and was OVERWRITTEN with a fresh key on every open. It fired on this container at 23:40:47 UTC 2026-09-21 during an audit `docker exec`. The REST process kept working from its in-memory key while its own DB became undecryptable on disk. Data fully recovered (at the time only content+metadata were encrypted; id/tier/timestamp/forgetting_json/entities_json/embedding were plaintext columns - entity names are encrypted since the 2026-09-24/25 pass) into db_recovered. FIXED AND DEPLOYED 2026-09-22: the running image no longer rotates the key, verified by comparing master.key checksums across a restart. Exposure at its peak was 117 records held only in one process's RAM; all were rescued. Since 2026-09-24/25 key loss is also guarded by MasterKeyMissing (no new key is created next to a populated DB) and MasterKeyMismatch (store_meta.key_id fingerprint checked on open).

local_mcp_note: mcp/server.py was rewritten onto the official MCP SDK (mcp 2.2.0). It previously spoke a homemade {"tool":...,"args":...} line protocol that no MCP client could talk to, and returned {"status":"executed"} for any unimplemented tool - 22 of the advertised 33 were silent no-ops. Now 29 tools, all backed by real implementations, verified end-to-end with the official MCP client.
local_mcp_store_note: Two modes, and the choice matters because the stores differ: bridge mode (`server mcp --remote http://192.168.1.183:8000`) sees the container's 120 memories and needs no password; local mode opens /home/skynas/.memcore (124 memories, password-protected) and is what .mcp.json selects today, paired with scripts/sync-rest-to-local.py. Both open cleanly and answer everything, so a client pointed at the wrong one looks healthy while serving memories nobody wrote. Always know which store you are on.

retrieval.mrr_note: UNVERIFIED project claim (grid search on LoCoMo + LongMemEval with real BGE embeddings). Never reproduced, and not reproducible on the hash fallback this deployment runs. Do not present it as a measured result.
retrieval.bm25_note: switched BM25Okapi -> BM25L 2026-09-22: Okapi's IDF hits zero at df >= N/2. The cached index rebuilds when any content changes (2026-09-24), not only on id/count changes.
retrieval.quality_note: top-3 precision on the live 120-memory store, 8 queries whose terms are present: 22/22 after the 2026-09-22 retrieval fixes, ~4/24 before. Re-measure rather than trusting this number.
retrieval.effective_weights_note: with the hash-fallback embedder the vector weight is 0 and its 0.35 share is redistributed: bm25 .385, graph .231, temporal .154, importance .154, metadata .077
retrieval.priors_note: temporal and importance are ranked only among memories the query-dependent arms (vector, bm25, graph, metadata) matched; a query none of those match returns []. Zero-weight arms are skipped, tier filters apply before truncation, and every result carries matched=true/false. Metadata ignores provenance keys (importance, imported_from, origin_id, id, uuid, hash, checksum, *_id), and on stores of >= 10 memories a token present in the metadata of more than half of them nominates nothing.
retrieval.rehearsal_note: recall rehearses only the top 3 matched results (1, 1/2, 1/3); only the top hit adds to the rehearsal count used for promotion. rehearse:false searches without strengthening.

embeddings_note: sentence-transformers/torch are NOT installed in the container or in .venv, so BGEEmbedder has always fallen back to LocalHashEmbedder while reporting 'bge-small'. The Dockerfile's `pip install -e ".[all]" || pip install -e .` hid the failure. Now one EMBEDDING_PROVIDER build arg, default 'local', and the build fails if the extras don't import. Reranker (retrieval/reranker.py) and Matryoshka embedder (embeddings/matryoshka.py) are experimental and NOT wired in; matryoshka_enabled/reranker_enabled default to false and nothing reads them. BGEEmbedder uses the model's own output dimension and refuses to start if MNEM_EMBEDDING_DIM disagrees; the hash fallback uses MNEM_EMBEDDING_DIM (384 here). Switching embedders later needs `memcore system reindex-vectors --reembed`.

deploy_procedure: bash scripts/deploy-skynas.sh [--keep-plaintext] [--drop-kg-hand-added] [SOURCE] - builds first, rescues through the API on every run, requires every live id in the store to stage, stops the container, tars the volume to BACKUP_ROOT/<stamp>-volume-before-deploy.tgz, compares the stopped volume with the rescue snapshot row by row (aborts and restarts the old container on any difference), stages only master.key/memory.db/memory.kg.db/vectors.vectors.json, recreates with --force-recreate. AFTER deploying this version: run `docker exec mnemosyne python -m memcore_memory.cli.main system reindex-vectors` to rewrite the sidecar; first open migrates entities and upgrades memory.kg.db one-way, so ROLLBACK = restore the pre-deploy volume tarball, never start the old image on the migrated volume.
blind_index_note: Worked for the first time on 2026-09-22. The tokenizer regex was written as '\b[a-z0-9]{3,}\b' in a non-raw string, so \b became a backspace (0x08) and nothing ever matched - every index written was empty. Live store reindexed: 120/120 rows carry a non-empty index. Reachable from the SDK and CLI (store.search_by_blind_index, `memcore memory search-blind QUERY [--k N]`, `memcore system reindex-blind`), NOT over REST or MCP.
